content.text: From Slack:
We've made another interesting observation. Although the Browser access to fcrepo/rest failed, we had no problems accessing it via curl. It might be something around the Browser authentication.

I had/have a lot of issues with the Repo via Browser (might relate to other problems and bugs) when working with Fedora. It works perfectly through the API and curl tho. I might suppose, it is not a good idea to trust the GUI? (in my case, bc. Fedora is behind a proxy and https is enabled).
A set of warnings appeared in the log around the time of the issue. Probably unrelated:

Not much to see here. The requested resource and all its children are resolved and IDs get translated. The only weird thing is that one of the resource translations occurs twice, on the beginning and at the end of the processing. All ends then with the known IllegalArgumentException.

It seems that the problem is occurring with increasing frequency. Everything is fine immediately after restart. Only the GUI is affected.
Another thing I was wondering about is why would Fedora start a transaction for a simple GET request?

Problem is that this should not be a singleton
PR -
https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/pull/2009

https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/commit/a64759643149ace9c48a7e8d2bdb65c65ee777ea
